items.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: a clean printed concept comparison sheet for the historical strategy game MicroCol, NOT a screenshot and NOT a production sprite atlas.
Input image 1 is only a reference for the existing warm hand-drawn colored game-art vocabulary and profession recognition. Redesign architecture substantially; do NOT copy its finished basic houses. The user requires drastically clearer upgrades.
Portrait large-format 2048 x 2736 concept sheet on flat light cream paper. Orthographic-like three-quarter front view from a consistent slight elevated angle for every building. Flat warm color fills with clear dark ink contours. No photorealism, no 3D render shine, no photographic textures. Plenty of whitespace between cells, thin unobtrusive grid lines.
LAYOUT: a small title strip, then EXACTLY 3 equal building columns labeled "I", "II", "III", and EXACTLY 8 equally spaced horizontal rows. A narrow left label gutter gives the short profession labels listed below. Single illustration in every occupied cell. Buildings stay completely within their cells; no overlap. First column illustrations must look poorer, smaller and more open than second-column houses; third-column buildings are visibly taller multi-storey complexes. Maintain a shared implied world scale rather than enlarging tiny shelters to fill their entire cell. No extra buildings or decorative thumbnails in the title or footer.
All row labels must be legible, plain hand-lettered and correctly spelled. Restrict in-image text to the supplied title, row labels, and column numerals. Empty cells contain only a short dash. No arrows or supplementary captions.
CRITICAL: a tier-I craft workplace MUST be just a minimal shelter with exposed essential equipment, NOT a little finished house; tier-II MUST be ONE STOREY, and tier-III industrial building MUST have TWO OR THREE STOREYS and look plausible around 1800. For civic/religious/defense/maritime buildings follow their functional equivalents specified in the rows. Show profession attributes as real objects, not floating symbols. No electricity, neon, motor vehicles, modern steel industrial sheds, sawtooth factories from much later industrial eras, modern guns or huge fantasy smoke. No people except the specified horses. No ornamental landscaping that distracts from the progression.

VISUAL TREATMENT: Closest to the existing game palette: economical warm ink linework, light cream plaster, honey-brown wood, terracotta roofs, cool grey slate. Stage I tiny rough open post-and-roof shelter, stage II modest whitewashed single-storey workshop with an exposed work bay, stage III orderly two- or three-storey brick-and-plaster early factory with repetitive tall windows. Restrained, clean and friendly; strong architectural size progression.
TITLE (exact): "1 / Cista linka / A"

Exactly 8 rows, row labels in this exact order. Each row has 3 level cells I, II, III.
1 TRUHLARSTVI: I open carpenter lean-to, sawbench, hand saw, wood shavings, a few logs. II simple one-storey lumber mill, large wooden waterwheel and sawn boards. III EMPTY, draw only a short dash, no building.
2 KOVARSTVI: I small open smithing lean-to, glowing little hearth, anvil, hammer, tongs. II humble one-storey smithy with low chimney, anvil visible through open bay. III large two-/three-storey early-1800 ironworks, masonry furnace chimneys, iron bars, tools and water-powered machinery.
3 ZBROJIRNA: I open arms workshop shelter, workbench, rack of period flintlock muskets and a few cannonballs. II simple single-storey armoury, muskets, cannon barrel, orderly powder barrels. III imposing multi-storey early-1800 arsenal workshop, broad doors, cannons, gun racks and cannonballs.
4 TABAK: I plain open tobacco-drying lean-to, clearly hanging golden tobacco leaves and one barrel. II low one-storey cigar workshop, drying leaves, rolling table and small cigar boxes. III multi-storey early-1800 cigar factory, many windows, tobacco crates and larger leaf racks, no modern machinery.
5 TKALCOVSTVI: I primitive open loom shelter with a visible wooden loom and small skeins. II single-storey weaving house with cloth, loom visible through open doorway. III multi-storey textile mill with many windows, wooden waterwheel and colorful folded woven cloth.
6 PALIRNA: I tiny open distilling lean-to with one clear copper still and one barrel. II simple single-storey distillery with copper pot and short brick chimney. III multi-storey early-1800 rum distillery, large copper stills and barrels, stout period chimneys.
7 KOZESINY: I open fur-working shelter, stretching frame and several clearly visible pelts. II simple ground-floor fur workshop with drying pelts under eaves and work table. III multi-storey fur manufactory with many windows, pelt racks and folded coats, no unrelated heavy industry.
8 TISK: I primitive open roof over an unmistakable large wooden hand printing press, type cases and sheets. II simple single-storey newspaper printing house with an open door revealing press and neatly bundled newspapers. III EMPTY, draw only a short dash, no building.
TOTAL ON THIS SHEET: exactly 22 distinct building drawings and 2 empty cells.
